This is likely the Palazzo della Cancelleria? Or Palazzo Venezia? Let me think. The first palace in Rome built from ground up in Renaissance style... Palazzo Venezia (begun 1455)? Actually Palazzo Venezia is considered the first major Renaissance palace in Rome. But the "first palace in Rome erected from the ground up in the new Renaissance style" — I recall it might be the Palazzo Venezia, built for Cardinal Pietro Barbo (later Pope Paul II), starting 1455, attributed to Leon Battista Alberti or Francesco del Borgo. Some sources say Palazzo Venezia is the first Renaissance palace in Rome.

Wait, but there's also the question of "from the ground up" — Palazzo Venezia was built from ground up. The Cancelleria was built later (1489-1513). So Palazzo Venezia seems right.

content.text:
**答案：Palazzo della Cancelleria（宗座文书院宫 / 大法院宫）**

这是罗马第一座完全从零开始、按新文艺复兴风格兴建的宫殿，建于约 1489–1513 年，由枢机 Raffaele Riario 委托建造（建筑师说法不一，常提到 Bramante 参与）。

依据：
- https://www.alamy.de/stockfoto-eingang-des-palazzo-delle-cancelleria-in-rom-italien-19135658.html（"the first palazzo in Rome to be built from the ground up in the new Renaissance style"）
- https://wcsiasc.org/formal-award-ceremony-12-of-october/（"the first palazzo in Rome to be erected from the ground up in the new Renaissance style"）
